title: Deep Learning Model to Denoise Luminescence Images of Silicon Solar Cells
mechanism: Supervised deep denoiser for luminescence images of silicon cells, replacing longer exposure or better cameras.
evidence: R: PSNR +30% and SSIM +39%, better than classical denoisers.
adaptation: Targets noisy CSIR cells (one test cell wrecks 1 run in 6). Use as a second channel or test-time variant only, since 7% of crack components are under 2% darker than surroundings.
min_experiment: Arm: two-channel (raw, denoised) at train and test, 5 seeds. Baseline: house. Metrics: comp>=20 px recall, crack IoU on CSIR cells. Kill: any drop in comp recall or no CSIR gain.

alt_notes.adaptation: Benchmark robustness split (simulated low-exposure / daylight EL on test cells) and optional denoising of noisy sources such as the CSIR_00070-type cells before inference.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Benchmark use: noise-degraded copy of the test set, report each method's drop. Optional arm: denoise then house inference vs raw on CV crack relF1@2; kill if < +0.005.

alt_notes.adaptation: Second input channel or test-time variant for noisy CSIR cells; risk of erasing the 7% of crack components that are less than 2% darker than surroundings.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: test-time two-channel (raw, denoised) model. Baseline: house. Metrics: comp>=20 px recall, crack IoU on noisy CSIR cells. Kill: any drop in comp>=20 px recall or no gain on noisy CSIR cells.
